faq.a: Eight weighted categories: keyword relevance (22%), section headings (12%), action verbs (12%), quantified achievements (12%), contact information (10%), ATS formatting (10%), length (5%) and date consistency (5%). Each is scored out of 100 and combined by weight. You get a gauge, a prioritised top-five fixes list, and category-by-category feedback. It openly states it is a heuristic, not a real ATS.

faq.q: What do the Lenient/Strict and min-keyword-length options change?
faq.a: Strict mode matches whole words only, so 'manage' won't match 'management'; Lenient matches substrings. Min keyword length (3–6, default 4) sets how short a job-description word must be to count, though short tech tokens written as acronyms or with + / # (SQL, AWS, C++, C#) are always kept. Keyword match is weighted by how often each word appears in the job description.

faq.q: Can it read a PDF resume, and what are the limits?
faq.a: Yes — upload a .txt or .pdf and the text is extracted in your browser using pdf.js; nothing is uploaded. It reads page by page with a progress message. Scanned image PDFs fail, because there is no selectable text, and it tells you to paste the text instead. The extracted text appears in the box for you to review before checking.

faq.q: What's in the Application Pack ZIP?
faq.a: Built with JSZip in your browser, the ZIP contains four files: ats-report.txt (the full scored report), resume-plain-text.txt (the extracted text that paste-your-resume portals expect), missing-keywords.csv (the job-description keywords you lack, with their JD frequency) and a README explaining each. You can also download just the report, or copy the missing keywords on their own.
